title: SSP-7 — Document Lineage And Publication State Delivery
summary: retain the shipped publishability cutover, exact selection controls, and initial lineage, New/Replace, Publish and Projects implementation evidence superseded by SSP-8
content_html:
SSP-7 — Document Lineage And Publication State Delivery

Status And Purpose

SSP-7 is closed as retained implementation evidence. Its publishable cutover, exact checked-selection action, initial lineage/New–Replace/Publish follow-through, and SSP-7.4 Projects presentation shipped. SSP-7.5 did not start against that model. DPD-1 — Immediate Public Projection Cleanup On Document Delete and SSP-8 — Revised Model supplied the replacement Delete boundary, Working-owned table, corrected Projects presentation, final verification, and durable transfer.

Started after SSP-4 — Collection-Aware Document Copy Delivery supplied exact configured collection Copy and analysis/works. SSP-7.0 — Document Lineage And Publication State Sanity Note confirmed the bounded implementation fit. SSP-7.1a — Publishable Contract Cutover Evidence completed the clean cut, SSP-7.1b — Set Publishable Evidence added the exact-selection publication gate, SSP-7.2 — Lineage And New/Replace Copy Evidence proved the initial private exact A-to-B table and explicit Copy choice, SSP-7.3 — Successful Publish Reconciliation Evidence proved the initial post-Publish public-URL update, and SSP-7.4 — Projects Publication Stage Evidence records the accepted initial Projects presentation:

A — Working document in dotlineform/projects
  -> 🟠 Pre-publish B in analysis/works (local)
       -> 🟢 Published B on the public site

A and B remain separate canonical documents. The public JSON is a projection of B and retains B's identity; it is not a third canonical document. SSP-7 does not compare content, present a diff, merge changes, synchronize A and B, or decide automatically whether a later Copy should create or replace.

Complete Outcome

One private persisted table records exact working-source, editorial-target, and current public-projection evidence. Its row grain is one exact A-to-B relationship. A may have zero, one, or several B rows, but every additional B is created deliberately.

Before lineage work, SSP-7 performs one coordinated clean-cut from the legacy viewable field to publishable. The new field exists only for a parent or child collection that participates in an owning public scope's Publish projection. Omission means publishable; publishable: false means exclude that document, and for parent trees its descendants, from the next scope Publish. Legacy viewable is removed from source, private projections, requests, packages, reports, configuration, and runtime state without an alias or dual reader.

The shared Docs management UI removes the legacy non-viewable control from Edit metadata and adds checkbox-aware Set Publishable… only to exact publish-capable parent Index and default sub-scope selection surfaces. It operates on every exact checked document and offers Include in next Publish or Exclude from next Publish with the selected count, OK, and Cancel. Local and local-external scopes have neither the field nor the action. If their pre-cutover audit reveals a real need to suppress local search or discovery, that becomes a separately reviewed discoverable contract rather than a hidden continuation of publication state. The existing scope-wide Publish remains unchanged and is still the sole public mutation.

When Copy to… targets a lineage-enabled configured workflow:

  • if no eligible B exists, New creates a fresh B and adds one table row;
  • if one or more B rows already exist, the author chooses New or Replace;
  • New creates another independent B with a fresh doc_id and another row; and
  • Replace requires selection of one exact existing B belonging to A, preserves B's identity and publication gate, replaces its source through the target's ordinary transformation, and updates that row's copy evidence.

Replace is an explicit destructive choice with preview and confirmation, but no content comparison or merge. It preserves B's doc_id, filename, added_date, exact collection placement, and current publishable value; it replaces the authoring content and transferable metadata, advances last_updated, rebuilds the exact target collection, and never publishes automatically.

The existing scope-wide Publish operation remains the only public mutation authority. After successful Publish, it checks exact configured editorial B public by-ID files and records {public_url} or clears publication in the small private row list. It adds no second Publish workflow, receipt extension, timestamp, generation hash, or special recovery protocol.

Persisted Table Contract

The delivery owns one schema-versioned private product at docs-viewer/data/canonical/document-publication-lineage.json. Its exact top-level contract and one illustrative row are:

{
  "schema_version": "docs_document_publication_lineage_v1",
  "rows": [
    {
      "source": {
        "scope": "dotlineform",
        "sub_scope": "projects",
        "doc_id": "A"
      },
      "editorial": {
        "scope": "analysis",
        "sub_scope": "works",
        "doc_id": "B"
      },
      "created_at": "2026-08-05T22:00:00Z",
      "last_copied_at": "2026-08-05T22:00:00Z",
      "publication": {
        "public_url": "/analysis/?doc=d-20260807-082735-54d9d5&subdoc=B"
      }
    }
  ]
}

Exact {scope, sub_scope, doc_id} identities are the only join keys. publication is null when B has no current public projection and otherwise contains only its exact public URL. The table never infers lineage from subject, title, filename, body, dates, selected row, current route, or public URL. It stores no copied body, content comparison, diff, merge base, semantic relationship, public timestamp/history, generation digest, or public Folder data.

The table is current operational evidence rather than report presentation. Copy and Publish own its writes through their confirmed mutation boundaries. The Projects report is its only presentation consumer. Rows remain zero-to-many by source and unique by exact source/editorial pair. If B later becomes unavailable, the row remains exact historical lineage and the report presents the target as unavailable without fallback or automatic repair.

Publication And Publishability Meaning

publishable is the canonical inclusion gate for the next scope Publish. Set Publishable… changes this source-owned gate for exact checked documents in an exact publish-capable collection without publishing. It is not proof that B is currently present on the site. Current publication is established only by the successful public projection recorded by Publish.

Local and local-external scopes have no Publish projection, so publishable has no meaning there. Their documents remain ordinary locally generated and discoverable Manage documents. SSP-7.1 audits and removes legacy local viewable values without translating them. Any intentional local discovery suppression is a stop-and-review signal for a distinct discoverable contract; it is not inferred from the old field.

The Projects report deliberately glosses over this eligibility detail and uses three simple stages:

  • Working — A exists in dotlineform/projects and has no B lineage target;
  • 🟠 Pre-publish — B exists locally in analysis/works and has no current public projection; and
  • 🟢 Published — B has a current public-site projection.

A B with publishable: false remains 🟢 Published while its prior public projection still exists. After the next successful scope Publish removes that projection, it becomes 🟠 Pre-publish. A newly copied, included, or excluded editorial B without a public projection is likewise 🟠 Pre-publish; Projects does not expose the finer eligibility distinction.

No stored generic stage field becomes canonical truth. The browser derives Working, 🟠 Pre-publish, 🟢 Published, and unavailable presentation from exact lineage and current publication evidence.

Report And Icon Ownership

The normal dotlineform/projects report uses the table to show publication progress beside working document A:

  • Working when A has no B;
  • 🟠 Pre-publish beside each current B without a public projection; and
  • 🟢 Published beside each B with a current public projection.

If A has B rows in more than one stage, both distinct cues may appear. Accessible labels and focused detail expose every exact B target and current stage without collapsing zero-to-many lineage into an inferred primary document.

The Projects report is the only publication-stage presentation surface. Its existing Folder, Work, and Series row icons are removed because Project State already owns that subject-route presentation. The analysis/works Manage report adds no publication-stage cue; its existing exclusion icon remains sufficient whenever publishable: false and retains the accessible meaning Excluded from next Publish. Projects does not need publishable in its stage projection. Local scopes show no publication-exclusion icon. Project State document icons remain unchanged: they show the Folder, Work, or Series subject route through which a document entered a Project State row, not publication progress.

Delivery Discipline

SSP-7 first replaces the ambiguous viewability contract with public-scope publishability and exposes that gate through shared exact-selection management. It then extends the existing configured Copy and scope Publish owners rather than creating a second transfer or publication workflow. The persisted table is justified because A-to-B identity cannot be reconstructed after Copy from subject, title, or public output. It is not a general provenance graph, activity log, document-version store, or report snapshot.

SSP-7.0 is a short scope-and-spec sanity gate. It confirms the current one-document metadata mutation, parent and sub-scope selection owners, Copy mapping/result, opt-in customisation boundary, exact replacement transformation, Publish changed/removed inventory, table ownership, and report seams before implementation. Each later step ends with focused evidence and an independent diff review.

Delivery Steps

SSP-7.0 — Confirm Scope And Delivery

  • [x] Sanity-check the legacy viewable mutation and generated follow-through, local/public semantic mismatch, exact parent and sub-scope selection owners, exact A-to-B mapping already present during Copy planning/apply, configured source/destination capability boundary, target-safe replacement rules, current scope-wide Publish preview/apply, public document inventory, and Projects/Analysis report composition.
  • [x] Freeze the table's exact owner, path, schema, ordinary post-rebuild write boundary, zero-to-many cardinality, unavailable-target retention, and public-isolation rules.
  • [x] Confirm the deliverables: clean-cut public-scope publishable, no local eligibility field, checkbox-aware Set Publishable…, explicit New/Replace choice, one persisted exact lineage table, Publish reconciliation, simple Working / 🟠 Pre-publish / 🟢 Published stages, focused evidence, and durable owner updates.
  • [x] Stop for review if the result requires content comparison, merge, synchronization, automatic choice, title/subject inference, a generic provenance graph, a second Publish workflow, or replacement of arbitrary documents outside exact lineage rows.

Checkpoint: SSP-7.0 evidence confirms the SSP-4 dependency, exact selection and legacy-viewability owners, the clean-cut public publishable replacement, local-scope exclusion, expanded migration footprint, table authority, destructive Replace boundary, Publish ordering, report row grain, risks, and stop condition. SSP-7.0 is complete. Stop before SSP-7.1a implementation approval.

SSP-7.1a — Cut Over The Publishable Contract

  • [x] Inventory every legacy viewable source value and read/write/projection consumer across configured repository and external-local scopes before mutation. Omitted and explicit-true values migrate to omission; public-scope false values migrate to publishable: false; local-scope false values stop for explicit review rather than becoming publication or discovery metadata.
  • [x] Replace viewable with publishable in public-scope source parsing, creation defaults, Copy target defaults, import/return validation, management records, parent/sub-scope build projections, search filtering, Publish planning, document packages, reports, configuration, shared runtime state, fixtures, and tests as one coordinated schema cutover.
  • [x] Remove viewable from local and local-external source and projections without replacement. After cutover, reject the legacy field everywhere and add no alias, dual reader, fallback, automatic discoverable field, or compatibility package parser.
  • [x] Remove the non-viewable checkbox and viewable payload from Edit metadata. Rename the retained public-scope exclusion icon/configuration and package/report choices to publishable / non-publishable terminology, with the accessible label Excluded from next Publish.
  • [x] Regenerate every affected configured scope and public projection, invalidate or regenerate in-flight package fixtures that carry the old field, and update current durable owner documents. Preserve completed SSP-4/SSP-5 delivery evidence as historical records rather than mechanically rewriting it.

Checkpoint: SSP-7.1a evidence records the 577-source migration, zero-file final dry-run, public parent/child false handling, local omission, regenerated private/search/public projections, five excluded public by-ID absences, 922 passing Python tests, and the passing 28-check Docs Viewer smoke profile. Independent review confirms no alias, dual reader, discovery replacement, selection action, lineage behavior, or unrelated workflow change. SSP-7.1a is complete. Stop before SSP-7.1b.

SSP-7.1b — Add Set Publishable

  • [x] Add checkbox-aware Set Publishable… only to the parent Index and default sub-scope list selection surfaces for exact collections that participate in their owning public scope's Publish projection. Preserve exact {scope, doc_ids} or {scope, sub_scope, doc_ids} ownership without route, title, filename, active-document, or displayed-row fallback; omit the action from local scopes.
  • [x] Show the exact checked-document count and one required option group containing Include in next Publish and Exclude from next Publish, followed by OK and Cancel.
  • [x] Add one focused atomic batch mutation that validates the exact collection and every checked document regardless of current value, removes explicit publishable: false for Include, writes publishable: false for Exclude, leaves already-matching documents unchanged, and rebuilds the exact parent scope or sub-scope once.
  • [x] Retain the exclusion icon in the parent Index and sub-scope report whenever current publishable is false. Do not invoke or alter scope-wide Publish.

Checkpoint: SSP-7.1b evidence covers public parent and sub-scope targets, one and several checked documents, mixed current values, all-no-op sets, stale or unavailable targets, atomic failure containment, exact rebuild ownership, modal copy, retained icons, local-scope omission, and unchanged scope-wide Publish. Independent review confirms no second publication workflow, per-document Publish, selection fallback, local discovery control, or parallel eligibility field was introduced. SSP-7.1b is complete. Stop before SSP-7.2.

SSP-7.2 — Persist Lineage And Add New/Replace Copy

  • [x] Add the schema-versioned private table and one validated, atomically written row per exact A-to-B relationship.
  • [x] Make lineage-enabled Copy planning return the exact existing B choices for A and require explicit New or Replace when a choice exists.
  • [x] Keep New on the existing fresh-identity transformation and add the exact replacement transformation that preserves B identity, placement, added_date, and publishable while replacing content and transferable metadata.
  • [x] Bind Replace to one selected current table row, exact target collection, and confirmed action; never fall back to another B or overwrite an unrelated document.
  • [x] Update created_at only for New and last_copied_at for New or Replace after the coordinated target mutation succeeds.

Checkpoint: SSP-7.2 evidence covers no existing B, one and several current B choices, unavailable retained B, explicit New, exact Replace, preserved editorial identity/placement/date/publishability, the ordinary targeted rebuild, small row-list follow-through, exact browser choice, and unchanged non-lineage Copy. Independent review confirms no diff, merge, sync, inference, generic overwrite, concurrency framework, or rollback extension was introduced. SSP-7.2 is complete. Stop before SSP-7.3.

SSP-7.3 — Reconcile Successful Publish

  • [x] Reuse the existing scope-wide Publish apply unchanged through its public file copy; add no second action, preview/receipt fields, or per-document Publish path.
  • [x] After successful public apply, inspect exact configured editorial B public by-ID files and set publication: {public_url} for present B rows or publication: null for absent B rows.
  • [x] Preserve the distinction between current public presence and B's current publishable gate; Replace never updates public evidence and Publish never rewrites A or B.
  • [x] Keep reconciliation as one ordinary small row-list write with no timestamp, generation hash, content digest, rollback, retry, or lineage-specific partial-commit response.

Checkpoint: SSP-7.3 evidence proves first publication, republish after editorial change, retained public B, removal, exact current public URL, unrelated-row isolation, unchanged Publish response shape, and public isolation. SSP-7.3 is complete. Stop before SSP-7.4.

SSP-7.4 — Show Publication Stages In Reports

  • [x] Project exact lineage/publication rows into the normal Projects report and render Working, 🟠 Pre-publish, and 🟢 Published without changing the report's document identity or selection owner.
  • [x] Resolve every displayed B title and Manage link through the current exact document-location owner; show unavailable targets explicitly and never copy presentation into table identity.
  • [x] Keep publishable out of the Projects stage projection: an editorial B without public evidence is 🟠 Pre-publish, while a B with current public evidence is 🟢 Published until a later successful Publish removes that evidence.
  • [x] Remove the existing Folder, Work, and Series row icons from Projects; keep those subject-route icons and copied clipboard text unchanged in Project State.
  • [x] Add no publication-stage cue to analysis/works or another public-capable scope report; retain its existing Excluded from next Publish icon unchanged.

Checkpoint: SSP-7.4 evidence covers zero, one, several, mixed-stage, Working, 🟠 Pre-publish, 🟢 Published, unavailable, exact Manage links, Projects subject-icon removal, unchanged Analysis exclusion ownership, unchanged Project State icons, and exact post-Copy/Publish source refresh. SSP-7.4 is closed as accepted evidence; SSP-8.4 owns the replacement Projects presentation.

SSP-7.5 — Superseded By SSP-8.5

SSP-7.5 was not started against the superseded v1 A-to-B table and per-target stage presentation. SSP-8.5 instead verified the current strict v3 Working-owned table, New/Replace, Working and Editorial Delete, Set Publishable, Publish, zero-to-many Projects presentation, direct non-lineage neutrality, and public isolation in one 162-test matrix plus focused browser smokes. It transferred the stable contract to current feature and architecture owners. No SSP-7 checkpoint remains open.

Not In Scope

  • content comparison, diff, merge, three-way merge, or selective updates;
  • automatic synchronization or propagation after A or B changes;
  • automatically choosing New or Replace;
  • replacing a B that is not an exact selected lineage target of A;
  • treating subject identity, title, filename, URL, or similarity as lineage;
  • one-to-one source cardinality or an inferred primary B;
  • automatic publishability changes or publication during Copy/Replace;
  • a local discoverable replacement or any other local visibility policy without a separate reviewed contract;
  • a new per-document Publish action or change to scope-wide Publish authority;
  • public exposure of A identity or the private table;
  • document version history, rollback, audit-event history, or a general provenance graph;
  • Project State subject placement or icons; or
  • SSP-5 Work/Series doc_url[], which remains derived from final published subject front matter.

Retained SSP-7 Evidence

These statements describe the implemented SSP-7 stages. SSP-8 is the current lineage and Projects-presentation authority.

  • Every initial displayed stage traced through one exact persisted A-to-B row and current successful Publish evidence.
  • Legacy viewable is absent as an active contract from current source, configuration, private projections, requests, packages, reports, runtime state, fixtures, and durable owner documents; explicit fail-closed rejection and migration evidence remain, and local scopes have no replacement publication field.
  • Set Publishable… owns exact checked-document publishability changes without publishing, and Edit metadata no longer presents the field.
  • New always creates a fresh B; Replace always preserves one explicitly selected B identity and current publishable gate.
  • A and B remain independently editable; later changes trigger no automatic propagation.
  • Publish alone establishes or removes current public evidence, and public JSON remains a projection of B.
  • The initial Projects report distinguished Working, 🟠 Pre-publish, 🟢 Published, mixed, and unavailable states without exposing publishability details or inferring identity.
  • Analysis retains its Excluded from next Publish icon separately from actual publication presentation; local scopes have no publication-exclusion icon.
  • Project State subject icons, semantic-token usage, SSP-5 public metadata, and public runtime remain independent.

Sub-Scope Publishing remains the feature router. Shared Docs source/build/management owns the public-scope-only publishable contract and Set Publishable…; SSP-4 owns the base exact-collection New-copy workflow; SSP-8 records the current Working-owned lineage result and durable transfer. Any later report redesign is a separate outcome, not unfinished SSP-7 work.
